cards.title: State and checkpoints
items: Reflex holds only a thread ID; LangGraph + SqliteSaver own all run state
One .rfdata/rfactory.db file holds checkpoints, Application rows, and the DraftVersion history
pending_gate() re-reads a live interrupt, so a review survives a restart

cards.title: Deterministic guards (no model)
items: Claim verifier: numbers and named entities in a rewrite must exist in its source bullet; 3 retries, then violations are shown
One-page trim loop drops the least JD-relevant item; after 8 attempts the overflow is shown to the human
Parse-back re-reads the PDF with pdfplumber (strict and lenient) plus optional pdftotext, flagging spacing risk
JD keyword coverage is scored on extracted text, because no ATS emits a score

cards.title: Model contract
items: One OpenAI-compatible client serves local LM Studio and any cloud endpoint; switching is a config change
Grammar-constrained JSON via response_format, thinking disabled, per-call token caps, one retry on invalid JSON, loud failure
LinkedIn and Indeed postings sit behind login or bot walls, so URL fetch is best-effort and the UI accepts pasted text

cards.title: Trust boundaries
items: Access control is the tailnet itself; a password on top of a private network is theatre, so there is no app-level login
serve.sh bakes the .ts.net host into the frontend bundle and keeps the Mac awake with caffeinate for the server's lifetime
The JD URL fetch is untrusted web input, best-effort; LinkedIn and Indeed bot walls make pasted text the normal path

cards.title: Human gates
items: interrupt() at resume review: approve, revise edited fields (re-render and re-score), or reject to re-enter tailoring with feedback
A second interrupt() after the cover-letter branch, then finalize records the application
Rejections reset verify and fit counters so retry loops cannot accumulate across attempts
